verses.text: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was sure he was right.
Then Elihu became very angry. He was the son of Barakel, from Buz, from the family of Ram. He was angry with Job, because Job made himself out to be right instead of God.
He was also angry with Job's three friends, because they had not found a good answer, and yet they had said Job was wrong.
Elihu had waited before speaking to Job, because the others were older than he was.
But when Elihu saw that the three men had nothing more to say, he became angry.
So Elihu son of Barakel from Buz said: "I am young, and you are old. That is why I held back and was afraid to tell you what I think.
I thought, 'Older people should speak. Those who have lived many years should teach wisdom.'
But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.
It is not only the old who are wise, or only the aged who understand what is right.
So I say, 'Listen to me. I will tell you what I think too.'
I waited while you spoke. I listened to your reasons while you searched for words.
I paid close attention to you, but not one of you proved Job wrong or answered what he said.
Do not say, 'We have found wisdom. Let God answer him, not people.'
Job has not argued against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
These men are shocked and have no more answers. They have nothing left to say.
Should I keep waiting now that they are silent, now that they stand there with no answer?
No, I will give my answer too. I will tell you what I think.
I am full of words, and the spirit inside me pushes me to speak.
Inside, I am like wine sealed up in a bottle, like new wineskins ready to burst.
I must speak and get relief. I must open my mouth and answer.
I will not take anyone's side, and I will not flatter anyone.
I do not know how to flatter. If I did, my Maker would quickly take me away.
